findings.observation: Sheets 3, 9, 19, and 21 show various electric infrastructure elements (existing and proposed) and contain notes addressing utility requirements and construction procedures. findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.16.0(1) is the foundational requirement for Land Development Review applications. A definitive statement that all electric infrastructure (existing and proposed) is shown is critical for applicant certification and Austin Energy review. The absence of this confirmation statement leaves ambiguity about whether the plans represent complete documentation or partial submittal pending AE approval. This statement is required as formal certification.

applicableAreas: Utility plan, electrical design plan, site plan
findings.observation: Examined Sheet 21 (Electrical Design Plan) for a note stating that all electric infrastructure is shown. Sheet 21 contains 'Utility Notes' (Block 6 from guide.md) with contractor directives to verify utilities but no note stating 'All electric infrastructure including existing and proposed is shown on these plans, or exceptions requiring pre-approval are noted.' The plan shows existing OHE, proposed transformers, and proposed routing but does not include a comprehensive statement that the electric design is complete.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.16.0(1) is the comprehensive requirements section for plan documentation. A standard practice and requirement is for plans to include a note certifying that all existing and proposed electric infrastructure is shown, and if anything is omitted or to be designed later (exceptions), those items must be noted with the requirement for AE pre-approval. This note provides AE Design certainty that the applicant has identified all infrastructure and indicates any gaps. Its absence means AE Design cannot verify the design is complete.

findings.comment: Note missing stating all electric infrastructure shown and exceptions require AE pre-approval. Add a note to the electrical design plan stating: 'All existing and proposed electric infrastructure required for service to this project is shown on this plan, except where noted separately or subject to Austin Energy Design approval.'
findings.observation: Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) is reviewed for the presence of a note stating that all electric infrastructure (existing and proposed) is shown on the plan or noting exceptions requiring AE pre-approval. The vision analysis of Sheet 21 explicitly confirms: 'No, there is no note at the top or anywhere else on the sheet with that specific phrasing or similar language indicating completeness of the electric infrastructure shown.' The sheet contains general utility notes (Block 6 on the blocks.md states 'Contractor shall verify horizontal and vertical location of existing utilities' and disclaimers about existing utility locations). However, there is no affirmative statement indicating that all existing and proposed electric infrastructure requiring approval has been shown on the Preliminary Electrical Design Plan, nor any notation of exceptions that require separate AE approval.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.16.0(1) requires that plans show 'All existing electric facilities (transmission/distribution structures, guys, anchors, transformers)' and 'All existing and proposed permanent structures' and 'Sufficient clearances demonstrated for existing and proposed electric facilities.' Without a note stating that all infrastructure is shown (or exceptions noted), reviewers cannot determine whether missing elements are intentional omissions subject to later AE approval or unintentional oversights. The Regulatory Overview section lists common violation patterns: 'Missing plat note requirements' and identifies that the grouping addresses 'what must be shown on plans to demonstrate a complete electric design.' A note confirming completeness or documenting exceptions is essential to that completeness demonstration. The title 'Preliminary Electrical Design Plan' suggests the design is not yet final, but even preliminary submissions must include a note about completeness or noted exceptions.

findings.comment: Electric infrastructure (transformers, meters, conduit, easements) verified on Sheets 2, 9, 19, and 21. Full coordination with landscape, grading, irrigation, storm drain, wet utility, and architectural elevation sheets cannot be verified without examining Sheets 10-20, 30-39. Electric easements shown on Sheets 2, 9, and 21 with consistent labeling; Sheet 19 legend includes 'E | Proposed Underground Electric' but shows minimal detail. findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.16.0(1) requires that electric facilities be shown on 'all required plan sheets' including landscape (for tree clearances), grading (for equipment location coordination), irrigation (for conflicts with underground facilities), storm drain (for utility coordination), and architectural elevations (for overhead facility clearances to buildings). Without examining landscape, grading, irrigation, storm, and elevation sheets, cannot confirm whether electric infrastructure is consistently shown across the full plan set and properly coordinated to prevent conflicts.

findings.comment: Electric facilities are not shown on all required plan sheets. The detailed design on Sheet 21 (transformers, meters, routing) must be repeated on: (1) Sheet 9 (Site Plan); (2) Sheet 11 (Grading Plan); (3) Sheet 19 (Utility Tap Plan); (4) Sheet 31 (Landscape Plan); (5) all other applicable utility, irrigation, and storm drain sheets. Ensure consistency in facility locations and equipment symbols across all sheets.
applicableAreas: Site plan, utility plan, landscape plan, grading plan, storm drain plan, wet utility plan
findings.observation: Examined all required plan sheets for electric facility depiction. Sheet 21 shows: existing OHE, existing underground lines, 4 proposed transformer pads, 7 meter locations, pull boxes, underground routing. Sheet 9 shows: existing OHE, one transformer pad, electric easements. Sheet 11 shows: electric easements only, NO electric lines or equipment. Sheet 19 shows: legend symbols for electric but NO actual electric facilities drawn on the plan. Sheet 31 shows: existing OHE on boundary, NO transformers, NO meters, NO underground routing, NO pull boxes. Vision analysis confirmed sheets 11 and 19 lack the complete electric design, and sheet 31 is missing transformers and staging areas shown on Sheet 21.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.16.0(1) requires comprehensive depiction of electric facilities across all plan sheets so all design disciplines can coordinate. Fragmented depiction creates risk of conflicts (e.g., landscaping in transformer staging areas, grading encroaching on underground routing, irrigation lines crossing conduit).

findings.comment: Electric facilities not shown consistently across all required plan sheets. Show all proposed electric facilities (transformers, pull boxes, meters, underground conduit routing, easements) on Site Plan (Sheet 9), Landscape Plan (Sheet 31), and Grading Plan (Sheet 11) with consistent symbols and locations matching Sheet 21 (Electrical Design Plan).
applicableAreas: Site Plan (Sheet 9), Utility Plan (Sheet 21), Landscape Plan (Sheet 31), Grading Plan (Sheet 11)
findings.observation: Sheet 9 (Site Plan) vision analysis confirms: 'Transformer Pad (Typ.) is explicitly shown and labeled on the west side... Individual meters, pull boxes, and detailed underground electrical conduits routing to the specific buildings are not visibly drawn or labeled on this sheet.' Sheet 21 (Electrical Design Plan) shows comprehensive electrical facilities (transformers, pull boxes, meters, underground lines) with explicit labels. Sheet 31 (Landscape Plan) vision analysis states: 'There are no clear labels or specific symbols explicitly identifying electrical facilities such as transformers, meters, or pull boxes on this landscape plan sheet.' Sheet 11 (Grading Plan) guide mentions 'utility easements' but vision analysis reveals electrical infrastructure details are not shown there. The grouping's Documents to Review section (lines 94-103) specifies: 'Verify all electric facilities and easements shown consistently across sheets' and lists 'Site Plan, Utility Plan, Landscape Plan, Grading Plan, Irrigation Plan' as required sheets. Detailed electrical facilities shown on Sheet 21 are not shown consistently on all other sheets where they should appear (particularly Landscape and Grading plans where transformer locations and clearances are critical).
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.16.0(1) requires plans to show electric infrastructure, and the grouping's common violation patterns specifically identify: 'Cross-sheet inconsistency: Electric facilities shown on utility plan but omitted from landscape, grading, or irrigation plans where coordination is critical (especially down guy anchors conflicting with accessible paths, trees conflicting with clearance envelopes).' The principle is that all infrastructure must be consistently shown on all sheets where coordination is necessary. The Regulatory Overview states (line 54): 'Cross-sheet inconsistency: Electric facilities shown on utility plan but omitted from landscape, grading, or irrigation plans where coordination is critical.' This project shows detailed electrical design on Sheet 21 but lacks consistent electrical facility depiction on Landscape (Sheet 31) and Grading (Sheet 11) plans, preventing verification of clearances, coordination with other site features, and staging area adequacy.

The presence of transmission easement notes on Sheet 3 confirms that transmission facilities are relevant to this project. The lack of documented submission of CAD files to AE Transmission Engineering represents a gap. AutoCAD drawings must be submitted in version 2016 or newer and include all relevant infrastructure crossing or near transmission lines.

findings.comment: Austin Energy Distribution Plan not verified as submitted. If modifications to existing Austin Energy facilities are proposed, provide a separate Austin Energy Distribution Plan showing detailed electrical design with plan and profile views.

This is a formal document prepared by or in coordination with AE Design. The Preliminary Electrical Design Plan on Sheet 21 shows the applicant's proposed routing and equipment, but this may not meet the requirement for a formal AE Distribution Plan if modifications to existing AE facilities are involved. Without documentation of existing AE facility modifications required, the necessity of this item depends on the scope of work affecting existing AE infrastructure.

The transmission easement and service extension to 8 buildings constitute AE facility modifications requiring detailed design. The preliminary status of Sheet 21 and integration with site plan (rather than as a standalone AE distribution design document) indicates this requirement may not be satisfied. A separate, detailed distribution plan with profile views showing cable depths, duct banks, transformer specifications, and service feeds is needed.

findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.16.0(1) requires that for all sites with proposed or modified electric easements, applicants must submit to Austin Energy a title commitment, title policy, Ownership and Encumbrance Report, or ALTA/ACSM boundary survey 'showing all easement encumbrances' for Austin Energy review to verify adequacy of existing easements and identify conflicts. The grouping guidance states to 'check: Document submittal records and Austin Energy coordination correspondence.' While the Master Comment Report clearly evidences Austin Energy coordination (dedicated reviewer, active Bluebeam comment link), the actual document submission cannot be verified from the available materials. The site plan documents themselves do not reference title documents, and the supplementary documents reviewed (Engineer's Summary Letter, completeness check results) do not document title submission. The existence of the Bluebeam coordination link suggests the applicant HAS coordinated with Austin Energy, but we cannot confirm what specific documents were submitted or reviewed from the visible materials.

findings.comment: Title commitment, title policy, Ownership and Encumbrance Report, or ALTA/ACSM boundary survey with certification showing all easement encumbrances not submitted to Austin Energy for review. Applicant must obtain and submit to Austin Energy a formal title document (title commitment, title policy, ALTA/ACSM survey, or Ownership/Encumbrance Report) certified to show all existing easements and encumbrances affecting the property.
applicableAreas: All proposed and modified electric easement areas
findings.observation: No title commitment, title policy, Ownership and Encumbrance Report, or ALTA/ACSM boundary survey certified to show all existing easement encumbrances is evident in the supplementary documents reviewed. The facts.md document identifies six existing easements of record (greenbelt access, drainage, wastewater, drainage, public utility, drainage) but does not indicate submission of a title document showing all encumbrances. The Project Review Form and Consolidated Site Plan Application do not reference submission of title documents to Austin Energy. Requirements per Land Development Engineering Review note that 'Current and proposed easements should be shown on all site plan sheets,' but no title commitment or ALTA survey is documented as submitted for Austin Energy review per UCM § 1.16.0(1).
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.16.0(1) explicitly requires submission of 'a title commitment, title policy, Ownership and Encumbrance Report, or ALTA/ACSM boundary survey' showing all easement encumbrances to Austin Energy for review to verify adequacy of existing easements and identify conflicts. This documentation is mandatory for projects with proposed or modified electric easements. The absence of this title document from the submittal package represents non-compliance with a foundational requirement for easement coordination. While facts.md documents existing easements, that internal research document does not substitute for the formal title document that must be submitted to and reviewed by Austin Energy.

findings.comment: Equipment symbols are inconsistent across plan sheets. Please establish a consistent legend for all electrical equipment (transformer pads, meters, pull boxes, disconnects) and apply identical symbols and labels on all plan sheets. Include the legend on each sheet showing electric facilities.
findings.observation: Examined equipment symbols across sheets. Sheet 21 uses: large blue rectangles with zig-zag symbols for transformers labeled 'Electrical Transformer Pad'; small blue circles with 'E' for pull boxes labeled 'Electrical Pull Box'; rectangles on building walls for meters labeled 'Electrical Meters.' Sheet 9 shows one 'Transformer Pad (Typ.)' but the symbol and style may differ. Sheet 4 (Existing Conditions Survey legend) defines 'TRANSFORMER ON PAD' with a square 'T' symbol. The symbols are not consistent across sheets in terms of graphical representation and labeling style.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.16.0(1) requires 'Equipment symbols consistent across plan sheets.' This is essential for plan reviewers and contractors to identify equipment reliably across all sheets. Inconsistent symbols create confusion and increase risk of misidentification (e.g., meter vs. disconnect, transformer vs. telecom box). All equipment of the same type must use identical symbols and labels across all sheets.

findings.comment: Electric facility locations do not consistently match across plan sheets. Please verify and ensure: (1) all transformer pads shown on Sheet 21 are also shown on Sheets 9, 11, 19, 31 at identical locations; (2) all meters shown on Sheet 21 are also shown on Sheets 9, 31 (landscape elevation); (3) pull boxes and conduit routing shown on Sheet 21 are shown on Sheets 9, 11, 19; (4) use consistent coordinate/dimension references to verify locations match across sheets.
applicableAreas: Transformer pad locations, meter locations, pull box locations
findings.observation: Compared facility locations across sheets. Sheet 21 shows 4 transformer pads at specific locations (NW, SW, central-south, central-east). Sheet 9 shows one transformer labeled 'Transformer Pad (Typ.)' on the western side, which may correspond to one of the four on Sheet 21 but location does not clearly match. Sheet 31 (Landscape) shows OHE but NO transformer pads, meaning the transformers shown in detail on Sheet 21 are not depicted on the landscape plan. This prevents landscaping coordination with transformer locations.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.16.0(1) requires 'Electric facility locations do not match across plan sheets' to be avoided. When the same facility (e.g., a transformer pad) is shown on multiple sheets, it must be in the same location relative to buildings, property lines, and other features. Discrepancies or omissions across sheets create confusion about the actual design and prevent verification of proper coordination (e.g., are trees within transformer access zones? is landscaping in staging areas?).
